title: Assumed Contract Rate Schedule for Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage Payoff Measurement
content:
**Rate schedule.** The assumed contract rate used to measure a lender's or lessor's payoff back to the loss date on a Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage total loss is set by how the vehicle was bought and how long it has been on the policy. For a vehicle bought new from a dealer (its physical damage took effect without a photo inspection falling due) whose addition to the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy is no more than 24 whole months before the loss date, the assumed contract rate is 5.9 percent a year; for a vehicle bought new that was added longer before the loss, 6.9 percent; for any other vehicle it stays 9.4 percent.

The vehicle's addition to the auto policy is the effective date of its vehicle-add transaction on the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy, or the date physical damage took effect on it when there is none. A vehicle bought new from a dealer is one whose physical damage coverage record shows no photo inspection due date.

| Vehicle | Whole months from addition to the loss date | Assumed contract rate, per year |
|---|---|---|
| Bought new from a dealer | 24 or fewer | 5.9 percent |
| Bought new from a dealer | More than 24 | 6.9 percent |
| Any other vehicle | Any | 9.4 percent |

## Boundary illustrations (hypothetical dates)

- Bought new, added on June 5, loss exactly 24 whole months later on June 5: 5.9 percent.
- Bought new, loss 25 whole months after the addition: 6.9 percent.
- Bought used (its coverage record shows a photo inspection due date), added 6 months before the loss: 9.4 percent.
- Bought new, no vehicle-add transaction on the policy, physical damage effective 30 months before the loss: 6.9 percent.
